notice: RN bank batch 149: Pediatric GI case studies: pyloric stenosis, intussusception, Hirschsprung disease and cleft lip and palate. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings of pyloric stenosis.

rationale.correct: Projectile non-bilious vomiting with an olive mass is pyloric stenosis.

questions.stem: Which parts of the preoperative plan should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Continue breastfeeding on demand until the surgery

options.text: Prepare the parents for what will happen
Surgery team aware in case of perforation
Give a laxative to clear the bowel

rationale.correct: IV, NPO, preparation and surgical backup.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: Which responses support the parent at birth? Select all that apply.

options.text: "This is not caused by anything you did. Let's look at your baby together."

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
